title: Evaluation & Observability
blurb: How you know your LLM product actually works — and how you keep knowing once real users hit it. Eval is a separate craft from training and serving; in 2026 it's a hireable specialty.

nodes.label: Task evaluations & public benchmarks
nodes.description: MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, SWE-bench, MMMU, the rest. What each measures, where it's saturated, how to read a benchmark table without being fooled.
nodes.doneWhen: You can read a model card's benchmark table and call out at least two ways it might mislead.

resources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
resources.author: Stanford CRFM
resources.annotation: Stanford's comprehensive benchmark suite. The leaderboards plus the documentation are an education in what benchmarks measure (and don't).

resources.title: lm-evaluation-harness
resources.author: EleutherAI
resources.annotation: The standard open harness. If a paper reports MMLU / HellaSwag / etc., it was probably this code.

resources.title: Open LLM Leaderboard
resources.annotation: Live ranking of open-weights models on a standard set of evals. Useful when you want a quick read on the field.

nodes.label: LLM-as-judge
nodes.description: Using a model to grade another model's outputs. Position bias, length bias, calibration, pairwise vs pointwise. How to make it actually correlate with humans.
nodes.doneWhen: You can set up an LLM-judge eval, measure its agreement with humans, and explain its biases.

resources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
resources.author: Zheng et al.
resources.annotation: The canonical paper on LLM-as-judge. Position bias, length bias, agreement with humans — the failure modes are catalogued here.

resources.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of LLM-Evaluators (aka LLM-as-Judge)
resources.author: Eugene Yan
resources.annotation: The practitioner's how-to: rubric design, agreement measurement, debiasing tricks. The post you'll send your team.

nodes.label: Golden datasets & rubrics
nodes.description: Building a small, high-quality eval set that catches regressions. Rubric design, inter-annotator agreement, the temptation to use the test set as a training set.
nodes.doneWhen: You can build a 100-example golden eval set with rubric scoring and use it to detect a deliberate regression.

resources.title: Task-Specific LLM Evals That Do & Don't Work
resources.author: Eugene Yan
resources.annotation: The pragmatic 'how to build a useful eval set' guide. Covers the rubric design and the failure-modes practitioners actually hit.

resources.title: Your AI Product Needs Evals
resources.author: Hamel Husain
resources.annotation: Why a small custom eval set beats every public benchmark, and how to build one. The 'start eval before training' argument in practice.

nodes.label: A/B testing for LLM products
nodes.description: Online evaluation: random assignment, novelty effects, what to log, why offline-eval wins don't always translate.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design an A/B test for a prompt change and pick the right success metric.

resources.title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments
resources.author: Kohavi, Tang, Xu
resources.annotation: The canonical reference for A/B testing in software. Applies to LLM products with the obvious mappings.

resources.title: The Practical Guide to LLM Evals
resources.author: Arize AI
resources.annotation: Covers the online-vs-offline trade-offs from a tooling vendor that lives in this space. Useful framing.

nodes.label: Tracing & observability (Langfuse, Phoenix, etc.)
nodes.description: Per-request traces, prompt/response logging, latency and cost telemetry, OpenTelemetry conventions for LLM apps.
nodes.doneWhen: You can debug a failing LLM request by reading its trace, not by re-running it.

resources.title: Langfuse
resources.annotation: Open-source LLM-observability with traces, evals, and prompt management. Self-hostable; widely adopted.

resources.title: Arize Phoenix
resources.annotation: Open-source LLM observability and eval, OpenTelemetry-native. The right pick if you already speak OTel.

resources.title: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions for GenAI
resources.annotation: The standard schema for LLM telemetry. Useful when picking tools or rolling your own observability.

nodes.label: Eval harnesses
nodes.description: lm-evaluation-harness, HELM, Inspect, simple-evals. The standard harnesses for running benchmarks reproducibly.
nodes.doneWhen: You can run a standard eval harness on an open-weights model and reproduce a reported score.

resources.title: Inspect — UK AISI
resources.annotation: Strong choice for custom-task evals; clean Python DSL, structured tracing, multi-model support.

resources.title: simple-evals
resources.author: OpenAI
resources.annotation: OpenAI's reproducible-eval harness for the benchmarks they report on. Useful as a reference implementation.

nodes.label: Cost monitoring
nodes.description: Per-feature cost dashboards, per-tenant attribution, tokens-per-request alarms, the cost regression that nobody notices until the bill arrives.
nodes.doneWhen: You can produce a per-feature cost breakdown of an LLM product on demand.

resources.title: LiteLLM cost tracking
resources.annotation: How the LiteLLM proxy attributes spend per key, model, and tenant. The pragmatic answer when you need cost dashboards yesterday.

resources.title: Langfuse — Cost tracking
resources.annotation: Same problem, the observability-tool answer. Choose based on whether you already own a proxy or a tracing system.

nodes.label: Continuous evaluation in production
nodes.description: Sampling live traffic, drift detection, human review queues, slice-by-slice quality dashboards. Eval as a continuous loop, not a launch gate.
nodes.doneWhen: You have a production eval loop that catches a quality regression within a day of it shipping.

resources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
resources.author: Chip Huyen
resources.annotation: Not LLM-specific but the chapters on monitoring, drift, and continual learning are still the best treatment of the production-eval problem.

resources.title: What We Learned from a Year of Building with LLMs (Part II)
resources.author: Yan, Bryan, et al.
resources.annotation: The operational section is the clearest writing on what 'continuous evaluation' actually looks like in a real LLM product team.

nodes.label: Pairwise human preference & Arena-Elo
nodes.description: Head-to-head comparison with crowdsourced votes, scored by Elo / Bradley-Terry. The Chatbot Arena pattern is the dominant 'real preference' signal in 2026 — the eval that everyone watches and the one no static benchmark can replicate. Adopt the pattern for your own product.
nodes.doneWhen: You can run an A/B between two model versions of your product as pairwise human preference, compute a Bradley-Terry score, and explain why the result differs from any single-rubric eval.

resources.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
resources.author: Chiang et al. (LMSYS)
resources.annotation: The paper that legitimized pairwise crowdsourced preference as an eval methodology. Read for the Elo-to-Bradley-Terry transition — that's the part most replications get wrong.

resources.title: Chatbot Arena: Benchmarking LLMs in the Wild with Elo Ratings
resources.author: LMSYS
resources.annotation: The launch blog post. Plain-language explanation of the pairwise / Elo / human-vote design. Pair with the paper for the methodology refinements.

resources.title: lm-sys/FastChat
resources.author: LMSYS
resources.annotation: The reference code behind Chatbot Arena and the LMSYS evaluation stack. Worth reading for the head-to-head session protocol and the vote pipeline.

nodes.label: Red-teaming & adversarial eval
nodes.description: Stress-test models against jailbreaks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and the OWASP LLM Top-10 failure modes. The eval discipline that complements clean-benchmark scoring with 'how does this fail when someone tries'.
nodes.doneWhen: You can run a focused red-team pass against an LLM feature and produce a triaged list of findings with severity.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
resources.annotation: The vendor-neutral taxonomy of LLM application risks. Use it as the checklist that anchors a red-team pass.

resources.title: Anthropic's responsible scaling policy & red-team practice
resources.author: Anthropic
resources.annotation: The clearest public account of how a frontier lab structures red-teaming against capability thresholds. Useful as the high-rigor reference point.

resources.title: PyRIT
resources.author: Microsoft
resources.annotation: Python Risk Identification Tool for LLMs. The open-source automation layer for running attack prompts at scale against your own systems.
